sentences.text: Kileskus is a genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur named after the Khakas word for "lizard," known from fossils including parts of the skull and hand bones.
Its skull bones resemble those of Proceratosaurus, sharing nares inclined at a 40-degree angle to the skull and a maxilla with a gently sloping posterior edge.
Although it is unknown whether Kileskus possessed a nasal crest, it is assigned to Proceratosauridae based on other distinct features.
The type species Kileskus aristotocus was formally named in 2010 by Averianov and colleagues.
Kileskus is considered an important discovery in 21st-century paleontology for understanding tyrannosauroid evolution.
Phylogenetic analyses have classified Kileskus as a basal proceratosaurid.
Kileskus lived approximately 166 million years ago in the Middle Jurassic, specifically during the Bathonian stage from 168.2 to 165.3 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
